name: fairy animals

attributes.attribute: a magical cow kept in Fairyland
a fairy horse that lived in the ocean
a seal that was really a person
tied to the fairies by their Otherworldly natures

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy animals are a folkloric motif. In Fairyland the fairies kept magic cattle, dogs, and cats. These creatures looked much like their kin in the human world. Fairy cows, black dogs, and the cat sìth all belong to this class. Wilder fairy animals also existed. They stood partly in this world and partly in the Otherworld. Fairy horses lived under the sea, such as the water horse. Seals that were really people were called silkies. Some were monstrous, like the afanc. Others were less frightening but still strange, such as the kelpie. These beings did not always answer to the fairies. Their Otherworldly natures still tied them to the fairy folk.

okr.objective: Fairy animals are the creatures the fairy folk keep and the wilder beings tied to them.
key_results: The fairies kept magic cattle, dogs, and cats in Fairyland.
Wilder fairy animals stood between this world and the Otherworld.
Ocean horses, silkie seals, the afanc, and the kelpie are examples.
These beings were tied to the fairies by their Otherworldly natures.
